messages.content:
You are an expert synthetic chemist planning experiments to maximise reaction yield.
Each experiment chooses one option for every variable listed. You will see the results
of experiments already run. Choose the next batch to find the highest-yield conditions
in as few experiments as possible. Use chemical knowledge (ligand and base effects,
substrate reactivity, solvent effects) and the observed results. Balance exploiting
good regions with testing informative new combinations. Never repeat an experiment.
Return JSON only.

Pd-catalysed Buchwald-Hartwig amination of 1-ethyl-4-iodobenzene with 4-methylaniline; choose the ligand, base and isoxazole additive.

Variables and options:
ligand:
L1: tBuBrettPhos [SMILES CC(C)C(C=C(C(C)C)C=C1C(C)C)=C1C2=C(P(C(C)(C)C)C(C)(C)C)C(OC)=CC=C2OC]

L4: AdBrettPhos [SMILES CC(C)C(C=C(C(C)C)C=C1C(C)C)=C1C2=C(P([C@@]3(C[C@@H]4C5)C[C@H](C4)C[C@H]5C3)[C@]6(C7)C[C@@H](C[C@@H]7C8)C[C@@H]8C6)C(OC)=CC=C2OC]

picks.reason: The close 3-methylisoxazole analogue gave 79.6% with L2/B3, so pairing it with the leading ligand may improve on that result.
This tests whether the lower-performing phenyl-substituted additive benefits from the top ligand and base.
Its ester placement matches the top additive, while the 3-methoxy substituent tests a close structural modification.
This regioisomeric methyl/ester isoxazole probes whether the favorable A13 substitution pattern is essential.
The ester-bearing isoxazole offers a close additive comparison with a different methyl and ester arrangement.
This tests whether an isoxazole-4-carboxylate can retain the strong performance seen with the A13 ester additive.
This ester-bearing positional isomer is a useful test of whether A13's advantage depends on its substitution pattern.
The related isoxazole carboxylate tests whether the ester remains beneficial without A13's methyl substituent.
This tests a simple methylisoxazole additive under the best ligand/base pair despite its different substitution pattern.
The dimethyl analogue probes whether additional methyl substitution helps relative to the simpler isoxazoles.
Repeating this close A13 analogue with the second-best ligand helps distinguish additive and ligand effects.
This provides a matched comparison to L4/B3 and tests the additive regioisomer with the established L2/B3 conditions.
This matched ligand comparison will reveal whether the alternative ester substitution pattern is ligand-sensitive.
This measures the effect of the ester position using the well-characterized L2/B3 catalyst system.
This tests a simplified ester-bearing additive against the established L2/B3 reference conditions.
A13 is the strongest additive, and this tests whether L4 can outperform the existing L2/B1 result.
This completes a useful ligand comparison with B1 while retaining the best-known additive.
This checks whether L3's weaker result with B3 is due to the base choice rather than the ligand.
This fills a ligand/base combination and tests whether the B2 penalty observed with L2 generalizes.
This more remote heteroaryl ester tests whether extending the A13-like isoxazole framework can further improve the leading conditions.
